clue.text: Give added strength to message poor meat-eaters won't want to hear?

definitions.text: message poor meat-eaters won't want to hear?
definitions.meaning: read as news that the price of steak has risen: beef's up

explanation.surface: A puzzling phrase asking for a bit of news that carnivores on a tight budget would dread.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase as a headline about the cost of steak going up.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce something is to make it stronger, an idiomatic phrasal verb with that sense.

clue.text: Someone coming in to give hospital department verbal attack

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A newcomer arrives at a hospital ward and lets rip at the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor or newcomer who enters is a person arriving, so the phrase is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Alien foe erring unexpectedly

indicators.note: something occurring unexpectedly comes in a surprising order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An enemy from another world makes a surprising mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien in its sense of someone from another country is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bear that smells horrible

definitions.meaning: the honey-loving bear of A. A. Milne's stories
an exclamation of disgust at a bad odour

explanation.definitionFit: Milne's Winnie the bear has this name, and the same word is an interjection made at a foul stink.

clue.text: It sounds like visible move

indicators.note: the clue says outright that what follows is heard rather than written

parts.note: something visible is in sight

explanation.surface: A remark that something seems to be a move that can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To move someone in the sense of stirring them to act is to provoke or stir them up.

clue.text: International monetary unit facing difficulties

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency unit

explanation.surface: A global currency is struggling on the markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in trouble is an idiom for facing problems or hardship.

clue.text: Army unit runs into police

indicators.note: runs goes into the police, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: cops are police officers
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A military detachment charges at the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A military body of soldiers, such as a signals division, is a standard army formation.

clue.text: Time to move quickly? Not moving having lost one wheel

parts.note: to run is to move fast

indicators.note: having lost says a piece is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: idle means inactive, not moving
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question about whether it is time to hurry, while something stalls after shedding a wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: IDLE losing I gives DLE. The definition is the last word, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trundle is an old word for a small wheel or castor, as on a trundle bed.

clue.text: Great golfer superior to these messing about

indicators.note: messing about with words suggests jumbling them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A top golfer is far better than these players who are just fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Oosterhuis was a leading British golfer of the 1970s, Ryder Cup player and later commentator.

clue.text: Was to blame for each favourite getting reprimanded

parts.note: per means for each, as in a pound per head
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
to rate is an old word for to scold

explanation.surface: Someone was at fault because each favoured child got told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To have committed a crime or misdeed means being responsible for it.

clue.text: Individually picking the best — in a way that may be very funny?

definitions.text: in a way that may be very funny?

indicators.note: picking is read as taking hold of, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: singly means one at a time, individually
the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: Choosing the top item one by one, in a manner that could be hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking' is read literally as taking in: the word for one at a time holds the best part. The definition's question mark flags that the adverb only usually means 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is chiefly heard in the phrase screamingly funny, meaning so amusing as to make people shriek.

clue.text: Men returning with Kate help with the group

indicators.note: returning means the letters for men go back the other way

parts.note: OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers or men
Kate Adie is a well-known BBC news reporter

explanation.surface: Soldiers come back with a famous reporter to assist the band.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Adie was the BBC's long-serving chief news correspondent, famous for war reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A road crew member who sets up kit for a touring band gives practical help to musicians.

clue.text: Attend to drunken son beset by booze

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: a drunk staggers, so the letters of son are jumbled

explanation.surface: Look after your inebriated boy who is surrounded by alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' gives ONS; 'beset by' puts the drink round it, so 'booze' is the outer piece, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To think carefully about or take notice of something is to give it attention.

clue.text: Worried, being defeated with leader bumped off

indicators.note: the first letter is knocked off the front of the word

parts.note: beaten means defeated

explanation.surface: Anxious after losing, with the team captain killed.
explanation.walkthrough: BEATEN loses its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten is used to mean troubled, as in asking what is eating you, so it means fretted or bothered.

clue.text: Biological groups sure began to evolve

indicators.note: to evolve is to change form, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Groups of organisms certainly started to develop.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxonomic ranks below genus are categories used in biological classification.

clue.text: Marine life form hurricanes unsettled — number finally destroyed

indicators.note: unsettled things are disturbed, so the letters are mixed up
destroyed says one letter is wiped out of the jumbled mix
finally picks the last letter of the word number

explanation.surface: Sea creatures are disrupted by storms, with many finally wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: HURRICANES minus R (last of 'number') is rearranged; 'destroyed' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiny echinoderm found on the seabed is a creature of the ocean.

clue.text: Highly-strung old lover that can be summoned to court?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

parts.words: that can be summoned to court
parts.note: citable means able to be cited, called to appear in court

explanation.surface: A nervous former partner who might be called as a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly-strung people are easily agitated or nervous, the same as being quick to get worked up.

clue.text: News from agent, nothing terribly great

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An agent reports that there is nothing very wonderful to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is journalism, the reporting of events, so it is the gathering of current information.

clue.text: Star terribly coy about nasty porn? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: about means surrounding, though the clue's last words swap which piece goes round which
quite the opposite tells the solver to reverse the roles: the second piece wraps the first
nasty suggests a mess, so the letters of porn are jumbled
terribly suggests disorder, so the letters of coy are jumbled

explanation.surface: A celebrity awfully shy about seedy films, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' gives PRON and 'terribly' gives CYO; 'Quite the opposite' flips 'about', so the second scrambled word wraps the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Procyon is the brightest star in the constellation Canis Minor.

clue.text: Dog crushed by big rock rolling over

indicators.note: rolling over says the hidden letters are read backwards
crushed by says the letters are squeezed inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dog gets flattened by a boulder tumbling down.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Dog crushed' as definition, but 'crushed by' is what signals the letters sitting inside 'big rock'; the dog is just 'Dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small Welsh breed of dog, famous as the Queen's favourite pet.

clue.text: They have top jobs in the construction industry

definitions.text: They have top jobs in the construction industry

parts.words: They have top jobs in the construction industry
parts.note: top jobs sounds like senior posts, but means work on the highest part of a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'top jobs' suggests executives; it means work done on the top of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen who lay tiles and slates on houses literally work at the highest point of the building.

clue.text: Our mistress, no maiden, is looking silly in traditional male garment

indicators.note: looking silly suggests something out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
no says the following pieces are taken out of the word before them

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Our lady of the house, no longer a girl, looks ridiculous in men's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: MISTRESS without M and IS leaves TRESS; with OUR it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are legwear historically worn by men, so they are the conventional menswear item.

clue.text: Father holding power, one over the church?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A priest with authority who oversees the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple's pointed top rises above the church building, literally standing above it.

clue.text: Solid curator

definitions.meaning: Sir Roy ..., director of the National Portrait Gallery and the V&A museum

explanation.walkthrough: Roy Strong ran two major London museums, the National Portrait Gallery and the Victoria and Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturdy thing is robust, and the museum director Sir Roy bears this surname.

clue.text: Horse is a timid creature, not half

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word is kept, here the front half

parts.note: a rabbit is a shy, easily frightened animal

explanation.surface: A horse is described as nervous, but only somewhat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is also British slang for 'very much', which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian is a famous breed of riding animal from the Middle East.

clue.text: Brighter lady involved with boy in audacious act of exploitation

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A cleverer woman gets mixed up with a lad in some brazen scam.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes blatant overcharging or a flagrant rip-off done openly.

clue.text: Student seen as 'home bird'

parts.note: in means at home
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A learner is described as a stay-at-home type, a homebird.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a trainee or a student gaining work experience.

clue.text: Part of body right inside animal

indicators.note: inside says the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: A section of anatomy positioned correctly within a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The chest is part of the human torso, so this is an example of a body part.
